pages.heading: Assessment Q2 — current through 2 Ω using Thevenin’s theorem

blocks.text: Find the current flowing through the 2-ohm resistor connected between the points \(a\) and \(b\) using Thevenin’s theorem.

items.title: Assessment Q2 — Thevenin bridge
question_paragraphs: Find the current flowing through the 2-ohm resistor connected between the points \(a\) and \(b\) using Thevenin’s theorem.

textbook_match.label: Exact textbook match
textbook_match.note: This class question matches prescribed-textbook Example 1.9.3 exactly. Open the canonical worked solution and its NRS figures rather than maintaining a second copy here.

blocks.text: For the source polarity shown in the question, \(V_a=7.2\,\text{V}\) and \(V_b=7.5\,\text{V}\), so \(V_{ab}=-0.3\,\text{V}\).
Therefore the current magnitude is \(47.8\,\text{mA}\), flowing from \(b\) to \(a\). If referenced from \(a\) to \(b\), \(I_{ab}=-47.8\,\text{mA}\).

blocks.label: PankusDesk verification
blocks.title: Why the direction matters
blocks.summary: The negative Thevenin voltage fixes the actual load-current direction.
paragraphs: The open-circuit result is \(V_{ab}=V_a-V_b=-0.3\,\text{V}\). That sign means point \(b\) is at the higher potential. When the 2-ohm load is reconnected, conventional current therefore flows from \(b\) to \(a\). The magnitude remains \(47.8\,\text{mA}\).
